name: Insurance
description: The end-to-end insurance experience across quoting, purchasing, renewing, and claiming.

stages.name: Awareness & Research
stages.description: The member realises they need insurance and starts comparing providers online.
actions: Read reviews and ask for recommendations
Visit raa.com.au to explore cover options
thoughts: How much should home insurance cost?
Is RAA competitive with other providers?
What cover do I actually need?

painPoints.description: RAA's insurance offer is hard to find and compare on aggregator sites. Members who start research externally often don't reach raa.com.au.

opportunities.description: Improve presence on comparison sites and ensure RAA's value proposition (member discount, roadside bundling) is clearly communicated at the awareness stage

stages.name: Get a Quote
stages.description: The member starts a quote online, entering property details and selecting cover type. Maps to Quote to Buy stages 1–4.
actions: Accept legal requirements and privacy notice
Select home use type and occupancy
thoughts: How long will this take?
Do I need to read all this legal text?
What material are my walls? I'm not sure.

painPoints.description: No indication of how many steps or how long the quote process takes. 8 of 8 participants in the August 2025 baseline study had no mental model of the journey ahead.
Two mandatory legal checkboxes must be ticked before proceeding. 7 of 8 participants tried to click Next without reading them and were confused by the red error state.
40% of users paused on the building information page because they didn't know their wall or roof material — this page takes 3x longer than any other.

opportunities.description: Add a progress indicator showing estimated time and step count at the start of the quote flow
Add photos or illustrations to wall and roof material options to help members identify their materials visually

stages.name: Purchase & Setup
stages.description: The member reviews their quote, adjusts cover and excess, and completes payment. Maps to Quote to Buy stages 5–8.
actions: Review contents cover and optional extras
Review and adjust quote (excess, sum insured)
thoughts: How much contents cover do I need?
Is this a good price? What if I change my excess?
Is everything correct before I pay?

painPoints.description: Members can't estimate their contents sum insured. The pre-filled $1,000,000 default feels arbitrary — 6 of 8 participants left it without understanding if it was appropriate.
The quote page requires significant scrolling. Average scroll depth is only 45% — more than half of users never see the coverage inclusions grid.
Adjusting the excess doesn't update the price in real time. Members must click Save quote to recalculate — 5 of 8 participants assumed the price updated automatically.

opportunities.description: Make the quote page a sticky summary card that updates in real time as members adjust excess and cover options
Add a contents calculator that walks members through room-by-room estimation with sensible defaults

stages.name: Ongoing Management
stages.description: The member manages their policy through My Account — updating personal details, viewing coverage, managing payment.
thoughts: What am I actually covered for?
How do I change my address?
Is my payment card up to date?

painPoints.description: Changing address requires updating it separately for membership AND each insurance policy. Not synced. This single issue generates 34 support tickets per month.
Policy detail pages show raw policy numbers and dates without context. Members don't know their excess without clicking through multiple pages.

opportunities.description: Sync address changes across membership and all policies in a single update
Add a summary card at the top of each product detail page showing excess, premium, renewal date, and cover level at a glance

stages.name: Renewal
stages.description: The member receives their renewal notice and decides whether to continue, adjust, or cancel their policy.
actions: Log in to review new premium
Decide to accept, adjust, or let lapse
thoughts: Has my premium gone up?
Why has it changed — I haven't claimed anything.
Can I get a better deal elsewhere?

painPoints.description: Renewal email doesn't show the new premium amount. Members have to log in to see the price — 18 support tickets in Q1 2026 were from members who didn't know their new premium until after auto-renewal.
No year-on-year premium comparison shown. Members can't see what changed between last year and this year without checking old documents.

No explanation of why the premium changed. 6 of 8 participants in the February 2026 test said the increase felt 'unfair' or 'unexplained' — all 6 said a simple explanation would have made it acceptable.

opportunities.description: Include the new premium amount and the year-on-year change in the renewal email subject line and body
Add a 'Why your premium changed' explanation with the contributing factors (claims history, market changes, property value adjustment)

stages.name: Make a Claim
stages.description: The member experiences an incident and attempts to lodge a claim. Currently all claims require a phone call — no online lodgement exists.
actions: Check what's covered (logs into My Account or reads PDS)
Navigate to 'Make a claim' in My Account
thoughts: Am I covered for this?
Can I do this online?
How long will I be on hold?

painPoints.description: Members don't know what their policy covers without logging into My Account and reading the PDS — exactly when they most need this information, it's hardest to access.
No online claim lodgement. The 'Make a claim' button in My Account directs to a phone number. 7 of 8 test participants expected a digital form.
Phone wait times average 8–12 minutes, rising to 18 minutes during peak periods after storm events. Claims call volume spikes 400% in the 48 hours after major weather events.

opportunities.description: Build an online claim lodgement form accessible from My Account that collects incident details, photos, and supporting documents
Add a 'What to do after an incident' guide accessible from My Account and the RAA app, tailored to the member's specific policy type

stages.name: Resolution & Recovery
stages.description: The member waits for their claim to be assessed, receives updates, and the claim is resolved.
thoughts: What's happening with my claim?
Who do I contact for updates?
How long will this take?

painPoints.description: No online claim tracking. Members cannot see the status of their claim in My Account. 6 of 6 interview participants said this was their biggest frustration — all had called multiple times for updates.
Communication is inconsistent. Some updates come by email, some by phone, some by letter. There is no single channel or claim history view.

opportunities.description: Build a claim tracker in My Account showing the current status, next steps, and expected timeline
Consolidate all claim communications into a single thread in My Account with push notifications for each update

insights.description: Claims NPS is -12 versus Quote to Buy NPS of +45. The post-purchase experience is dramatically worse than pre-purchase, suggesting RAA's digital investment has focused on acquisition over retention.

Address changes must be updated separately across membership and every insurance policy. This single pain point generates 34 support tickets per month — the highest-volume complaint category for My Account.
The digital experience drops off sharply after purchase. Quote to Buy has 8 fully digital stages; Claims has 0 — lodgement requires a phone call. This is a structural gap in the digital experience.
Conversion from quote page to purchase is 23% against an industry average of 31%. The 8 percentage point gap represents approximately $2.4M in annual premium.

22 support calls in Q4 2025 were members wanting to adjust their cover at renewal but finding no online option. Average call duration was 12 minutes — this is a high-cost, easily avoidable support touchpoint.

Members with 3 or more products spend 40% longer on the My Account dashboard than single-product members, suggesting the product list becomes harder to navigate at scale — a retention risk for the most valuable segment.

changelog.description: Parent journey map created with aggregated data across Quote to Buy, Renewals, and Claims
